text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where code changes are automatically built and tested frequently. Instead of waiting until the end of a project, developers merge their work into a shared repository several times a day. Each time, a CI pipeline kicks in: it compiles the code, runs automated builds, and executes a full suite of tests. The main goal is to catch issues early, before they become complex and expensive to fix. If a build fails or a test breaks, the team is notified immediately, allowing them to correct the problem right away. This leads to more stable software and faster, safer releases.
